w10_P4_000305: A packing line drives a carton of 59000 grams along its rollers. The rate at which the drive's acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 3t^2 + 6t, and between t = 2 seconds and t = 3 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval. From the value reached at the end the engineer subtracts a slip allowance of 3 and then adds a gearbox contribution of 26, giving the acceleration in metres per second squared that the carton actually experiences. The controller works out the force needed for that acceleration and expresses it in kilonewtons. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000313: A teaching laboratory launches a trolley of 12 kg along a level rail. The trolley's launch speed in metres per second is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. The bench records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion, multiplies it by 6 for the 6 launches in a demonstration, and multiplies that by 11 for the 11 demonstrations in the term. A fixed instrument allowance of 16 J is then added, and the total is multiplied by 12 because 12 laboratories run the same course. The rail is 3 m long, a length the bench never uses. What total, in joules, does the department record?
w10_P4_000319: A test report ends with a value in kilojoules, converted from a figure that is 2 times a single-shot reading, since two rigs fire together. The single-shot reading is what remains after a friction allowance of 4 J is subtracted from the energy a slug of 51000 grams carries because of its motion. The slug's speed in metres per second is 7 times the sum of 3 and 3. The rig's barrel is 2 m long, a dimension the report notes but never uses. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000323: A rail test bench launches a carriage of 24000 grams. Its launch speed in metres per second is found by taking 5 times the sum of 2 and 17 and then subtracting a slip loss of 20 from the result. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. From the converted figure a contractual credit of 2 kJ is subtracted, and a standing allowance of 10 kJ is added afterwards. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000324: A haulage ledger ends with a number that is 13 kN more than a value, and that value was itself 15 kN more than a converted reading. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to drive a wagon of 92 kg, less a coupling tare of 1 N taken off before the conversion. The wagon's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 2t^2 + 5t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. The siding is 60 m long, a distance the ledger never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the ledger?
w10_P4_000331: An air-gun on a laboratory bench fires a slug of 4000 grams. The slug's muzzle speed in metres per second is 12 times the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0. The bench records the energy the slug carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. Because the programme calls for 7 identical shots, the converted figure is multiplied by 7. The gun's barrel is 1.2 m long, a dimension the bench never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000332: A workshop ledger ends with a number that is 8 kN more than a figure that was itself 6 times an adjusted reading, since 6 benches contribute. The adjusted reading is a converted force with a contractual credit of 28 kN subtracted from it. That converted force is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a test mass of 3000 grams on the bench, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is 4 times the sum of 2 and 3. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the ledger?
w10_P4_000334: A calibration rig carries 8 identical reference blocks, and its routine works through every distinct group of 4 that can be chosen from them. The number of such groups is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration the rig applies to a shuttle of 65000 grams. The controller works out the force needed to drive the shuttle and expresses it in kilonewtons, then subtracts a frame tare of 1 kN and adds a fixed mounting allowance of 12 kN. The result is multiplied by 5, because 5 rigs run the same routine. The rig bed is 2 m long, a dimension that plays no part. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?
w10_P4_000336: A laboratory report ends with a value found by adding a standing instrument allowance of 19 kJ to a converted total. That converted total is the kilojoule form of a figure that is 3 times the energy of a single release, since 3 releases make a set. In one release a glider of 54000 grams slides along the track, and its release speed in metres per second is the largest whole number that divides both 234 and 167 exactly, with nothing left over. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000341: A conveyor report ends with a figure that is 5 times the force needed for one push, because 5 pushers act together. Each push accelerates a crate of 160000 grams along the belt. The acceleration in metres per second squared is worked out from the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 12, to which a drive contribution of 4 is added and from which a friction loss of 24 is then subtracted. What figure, in newtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000342: A vibration bench fits the curve 1x^3 - 5x^2 to a recorded trace, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 2 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a test mass of 49000 grams on the shaker head. The bench records the energy the mass carries because of its motion, subtracts a damping allowance of 10 J, and expresses the remainder in kilojoules. That converted figure is multiplied by 5 for the 5 heads on the machine, and a fixed calibration offset of 1 kJ is added at the end. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000350: A quarry ledger closes with a number that is 20 N more than a site total. The site total is 9 times a line figure, and the line figure is 3 times a station value, since 9 lines and 3 stations are involved. Each station value is what you get by adding a bearing preload of 27 N to the force needed to accelerate a hopper of 178 kg. The hopper's acceleration in metres per second squared is the largest whole number that divides both 96 and 20 exactly, with nothing left over. What number, in newtons, closes the ledger?
w10_P4_000354: A drop-test laboratory keeps 9 identical reference masses and tests every distinct pair that can be chosen from them. The number of such pairs is, in metres per second, the release speed of a carrier of 53000 grams on the laboratory's rail. The bench records the energy the carrier carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. It then subtracts a rig allowance of 19 kJ and, after that, a further handling allowance of 10 kJ. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000356: A workshop record ends with a number found by taking 4 kJ off a figure that is 6 times a converted reading, since 6 benches contribute. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of a value obtained by adding a fixed instrument offset of 1 J to the energy a carrier of 32 kg holds because of its motion. The carrier's speed in metres per second is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 4x + 3 = 0. What number, in kilojoules, ends the record?
w10_P4_000357: A press-shop summary ends with a number found by taking a contractual credit of 12 kN off a converted total. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure that is 12 times the force needed for one stroke, since 12 strokes make a cycle. In one stroke a tool of 25000 grams is accelerated, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 4t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the summary?
w10_P4_000361: A depot receives 256 crates on one lorry and 371 on another, and the supervisor works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. That number is, in metres per second squared, the acceleration his tug gives to a load of 110 kg. The control system works out the force needed to move the load, expresses it in kilonewtons, and adds a fixed rigging allowance of 9 kN. The result is then multiplied by 5, because 5 tugs work the yard. Each lorry bed is 12 m long, a dimension the control system never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the control system report?
w10_P4_000366: A launcher brings a carriage of 23 kg up to speed along a level track, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 4t^2 + 8t. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the one recorded. The logger records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed and multiplies it by 3 for the 3 carriages in a run, by 2 for the 2 runs in a session, and by 10 for the 10 sessions in the programme. The programme total is then expressed in kilojoules. The track is 80 m long, a length the logger never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the logger report?
w10_P4_000371: A crane report ends with a number that is 19 kN more than a figure, and that figure was itself 17 kN more than a converted reading. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a hook load of 128 kg, less a rigging tare of 1 N taken off before the conversion. The load's acceleration in metres per second squared is the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0. The crane's jib is 20 m long, a dimension the report never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000376: A teaching bench launches a trolley of 51 kg along a level rail. The trolley's launch speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. The bench records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 2, because 2 trolleys are launched together. A fixed instrument offset of 7 J is added, and the total is then expressed in kilojoules. The rail stands 0.8 m above the floor, a height the bench never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?
w10_P4_000378: A test summary ends with a number found by taking a calibration credit of 1 kJ off a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of a value obtained by adding a fixed instrument offset of 21 J to the energy a projectile of 41000 grams carries because of its motion. The projectile's speed in metres per second is found by taking the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0 and adding a drive contribution of 17 to it. What number, in kilojoules, ends the summary?
w10_P4_000393: A haulage report ends with a number that is 24 kN more than a figure, and that figure was itself 25 kN more than a converted reading. The converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a wagon of 157000 grams along the siding. The wagon's acceleration in metres per second squared is 2 times the sum of 6 and 4. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?
w10_P4_000394: A test facility publishes a number that is 10 times a site figure, because 10 sites run the same programme. Each site figure is 9 times a converted single-run reading, since 9 runs make a site programme. The converted reading is the kilojoule form of the energy a sled of 21 kg carries because of its motion at the end of a run. During a run the sled's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 5t^2 + 5t between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds, and the sled starts from rest at t = 0 seconds, with t the time in seconds. The facility's track is 120 m long, a length that never enters the energy account. What number, in kilojoules, does the facility publish?
w10_P4_000406: A demonstration rig on a lecture bench launches a puck of 2 kg across a smooth surface. The puck's launch speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 7x + 10 = 0. The bench records the energy the puck carries because of its motion and adds a fixed instrument offset of 25 J to the record. That sum is multiplied by 10, because 10 launches make a demonstration, and the total is expressed in kilojoules. The demonstration is repeated in 6 lecture theatres, and the converted totals are added, giving the departmental figure. The bench is 1.4 m wide, a dimension that plays no part. What is the departmental figure, in kilojoules?
w10_P4_000417: A laboratory report ends with a value that is 2 times a converted reading, because two benches contribute equally. That converted reading is the kilojoule form of a figure obtained by subtracting a bearing allowance of 4 J and then a drag allowance of 7 J from the energy a carrier of 21000 grams holds because of its motion. The carrier's speed in metres per second is the total of the squares of the whole numbers from 1 to 4. What value, in kilojoules, ends the report?
w10_P4_000422: A drone workshop fits the curve 2x^3 - 1x^2 to a flight trace, with x the elapsed time in seconds. At the instant x = 4 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a payload of 11000 grams. The workshop records the energy the payload carries because of its motion, subtracts a telemetry allowance of 30 J, adds a calibration offset of 8 J, and then subtracts a handling allowance of 7 J. The result is multiplied by 7, because 7 payloads fly the same profile. What figure, in joules, does the workshop report?
